keyFindings.description: push-main now pushes `HEAD:refs/heads/main` (base: `git push origin main`) and, after a rejection, rebases the whole checkout onto main (:429) and pushes again. The three npm publish jobs run on a workflow_dispatch from any branch (release.yaml:526/702/889, no ref gate; the spec keeps that) and check out the event's ref (release.yaml:614-617, no `ref:`), so a branch dispatch lands that branch's commits on main through the deploy key with a `[skip ci]` head commit (release.yaml:672), bypassing main's ruleset and starting no workflow. Reproduced: from a branch two commits ahead, the base refspec pushes nothing; the new one fast-forwards main to the branch. The 'callers check out detached' premise (release-push.sh:63,405; release-push.test.sh:327) describes no caller of push-main. Fix: refuse unless HEAD is exactly one commit over main's tip (re-checked after each rebase), with a harness case pinning it.

The checker scans each job's own text (`texts_of(job)`) and only the step's own `shell:` (:283), so a workflow-level `env: DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}` or `defaults: run: shell: python` leaves it green while every build job then holds the key or runs an unread interpreter; `write_scopes` (:301) already inherits the workflow's permissions, so this is the one inheritance the file misses. Reproduced on copies of the real release.yaml by both thermonuclear agents.

DEPLOY_KEY_REF and DEPLOY_KEY_VALUE are case-sensitive while OTHER_SECRET (:109) is IGNORECASE with the comment that secret names are case-insensitive; `secrets.deploy_key` makes a job with the key and no write scope a plain job and escapes rule 1d. One `re.IGNORECASE`.

No `## Contract change census` although the PR changes release-push.sh's contract at a process boundary (`tag` pushes nothing; `push-main` requires DEPLOY_KEY and GITHUB_REPOSITORY; new `version`/`no-credential` refusals; the checker's refusal in the required lint job). Callers found: the three workflows only (release.yaml:671/682/696, 861/870/884, 1054/1063/1077; listener :279/:535/:607; infra :120/:285), all migrated. The census lists them with dispositions and names the rollout as an immediate refusal closing the deploy-key exposure.
`npm publish` is allowed whatever its arguments, so a publish with no tarball path (a directory publish, which runs prepack) passes in a credentialed job; allow `publish` only with a `.tgz` argument.

The tripwire step may carry `continue-on-error: true` unrefused, and the header (:20-21) says 'with no if:, so the tripwire always runs', which is false: a failed earlier step skips it. Refuse continue-on-error as `if:` is refused; correct the sentence.

deploy_key_env's `:?` guards exit without the file's `::error::` sink or fail_outstanding's summary, so push-main with no DEPLOY_KEY gives no annotation and no 'the release itself succeeded' sentence; the test at release-push.test.sh:324 only checks the text names DEPLOY_KEY.

`git tag -l | head -1` now runs under `set -o pipefail`; once the listing exceeds the pipe buffer, head's early exit gives git SIGPIPE and the shared version step dies with nothing on stdout. Not reachable at today's tag counts; `git for-each-ref --count=1 --sort=-v:refname` removes the pipe.
